summary_html: Child achieves **permanency through legal guardianship** or kinship care. Federal programs provide funding parity with adoption for approved relatives.

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court held that a parent may voluntarily transfer permanent legal and physical custody to a relative for good cause, but that on this record the earlier transfer was involuntary and therefore triggered the presumption of palpable unfitness.
key_cases.relevance: It defines the standard and the consequences of kinship permanency by transfer of permanent legal and physical custody.
key_cases.quote: because such a transfer of custody is a statutorily approved permanency disposition, we conclude that a parent may voluntarily transfer custody to a relative for good cause

key_cases.holding: The court held that the permanency statute's bar on long-term foster care for children under twelve is unambiguous and does not conflict with the best-interests standard, and that the termination statute requires no finding on a child's adoptability.
key_cases.relevance: It explains when long-term foster care is and is not an available permanency option under Minnesota's permanency statute.
key_cases.quote: we hold that the termination statute does not require assessment of a child's adoptability

key_cases.holding: The court held that good cause to depart from ICWA's placement preferences must rest on one or more of the BIA guideline factors and that a child's need for stability is not equivalent to a need to be adopted, reversing the non-Indian adoptions.
key_cases.relevance: It constrains the good-cause showing needed to place an Indian child outside the statutory preference order in a permanency disposition.
key_cases.quote: We hold, while good cause may include a child's need for stability, this is not equivalent to a need to be adopted.

key_cases.case_name: In re Petition to Adopt S.T.
key_cases.holding: The court held that the trial court had jurisdiction over the foster parents' adoption petition even without the Commissioner's consent, rejecting the agency's claim of an absolute veto over placement.
key_cases.relevance: It preserves a court's authority to decide permanency for a child in agency custody over the agency's objection.
key_cases.quote: we hold that subdivision 7 grants the trial court jurisdiction over the adoption proceeding absent the Commissioner's consent to an adoption petition

key_cases.holding: Affirming adoption by the child's grandparents over the competing petition of her long-term foster parents, the court declined to reach the equal-protection challenge to the minority-heritage preference statute and held instead that adoptive placement with a relative is presumptively in a child's best interests unless good cause to the contrary or detriment to the child is shown.
key_cases.relevance: It sets the standard when a relative and a non-relative both seek permanency for the same child, and holds that the temporary pain of separating a securely attached child from a good foster home is not good cause to defeat the family preference.
key_cases.quote: adoptive placement with a family member is presumptively in the best interests of a child, absent a showing of good cause to the contrary or detriment to the child

state_agency.name: Minnesota Department of Children, Youth, and Families
state_agency.hotline: No statewide hotline. Call the county or Tribal child protection agency where the child lives — the directory link is on dcyf.mn.gov/individuals-and-families/report-abuse

extended_foster_care_age: To age 21 (voluntary; youth must meet one of five eligibility conditions; re-entry to 21 allowed; Minn. Stat. § 260C.451)

common_failures: Failure to prove unfitness by clear and convincing evidence
Santosky v. Kramer standard not met

timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Must file TPR or document compelling reason

timeline_requirements.starts_from: The child's placement out of the home of the parent or guardian from whom the child was removed
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Not specified in Minn. Stat. § 260C.204; subd. 1 requires the court to hold the permanency progress hearing no later than six months after the child's placement, and subd. 4(a)(2) lets the court continue the matter no more than six additional months before a hearing under §§ 260C.503 to 260C.521.
